'''Walter Wahli''', born on 23 May 1946 in Moutier, Switzerland, is a distinguished biologist and professor.  He has held academic positions at the [[University of Lausanne]] and at [[Nanyang Technological University|Nanyang Technological University of Singapore]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.metabolomicsconference.com/speaker/2017/walter-wahli-nanyang-technological-university-singapore|title=Walter Wahli {{!}} Metabolomics Congress 2017 {{!}} Conferenceseries|website=www.metabolomicsconference.com|date=8 May 2017 |language=en|access-date=2019-10-24}}</ref> Wahli's research has contributed to the understanding of metabolic regulation through [[gene expression]]. He is particularly recognized for his work on nuclear receptors, specifically the [[Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor|Peroxisome proliferator-activated Receptors]] (PPARs), which play a crucial role in regulating the body's energy balance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genomyx.ch/fbm-awardees-2011/|title=FBM Awardees 2011|website=www.genomyx.ch|access-date=2019-10-24}}</ref>

== Education ==
Wahli received his Ph.D. in Biological Sciences from the [[University of Bern]] in [[Switzerland]]. He then worked as a post-doctoral researcher at the Department of Embryology, [[Carnegie Institution for Science|Carnegie Institution of Washington]] in [[Baltimore]], and as a visiting fellow and a visiting associate at the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH), [[National Cancer Institute]], [[Bethesda, Maryland]], US.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.swir.ch/en/programme/99-der-rat/579-prof-dr-walter-wahli-en|title=Prof. Dr. Walter Wahli|website=www.swir.ch|access-date=2019-10-24}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 1980, Wahli became full professor and the director of the Institute of Animal Biology at the [[University of Lausanne]] where he completed several mandates, such as vice-rector for research, postgraduate and continuing education and founding director of the Center for Integrative Genomics. He then served as a professor of metabolic disease at the [[Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine]], a joint medical school of Nanyang Technological University Singapore and [[Imperial College London]], in Singapore. Since 2019, he is a visiting professor at this school.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://applicationspub.unil.ch/interpub/noauth/php/Un/UnPers.php?PerNum=4088&LanCode=37|title=Unisciences – UNIL – Walter Wahli|website=applicationspub.unil.ch|access-date=2019-10-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unil.ch/cig/en/home/menuinst/about.html|title=About|website=www.unil.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-10-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unil.ch/cig/en/home/menuinst/research/professors-emeritus/prof-wahli.html|title=Prof. Wahli|website=www.unil.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-10-24}}</ref>

Wahli has a long-standing interest in nuclear receptors found within cell nuclei which are responsible for sensing [[steroid hormone]]s, [[fatty acid]]s and other [[Lipophilicity|lipophilic]] molecules. Upon activation by these ligands, the receptors regulate the expression of specific genes, thereby controlling key biological processes, such embryonic development, [[homeostasis]], and metabolism of the vertebrates.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wahli|first1=W|last2=Martinez|first2=E|date=1991-06-01|title=Superfamily of steroid nuclear receptors: positive and negative regulators of gene expression.|journal=The FASEB Journal|volume=5|issue=9|pages=2243–2249|doi=10.1096/fasebj.5.9.1860615|doi-access=free|pmid=1860615|s2cid=1464261|issn=0892-6638}}</ref> Since 1977, Wahli reported several discoveries related to the molecular mechanism of action of the estrogen receptor and then of the fatty acid-activated [[Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor|peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs)]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wahli|first=Walter|title=Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs): from metabolic control to epidermal wound healing|journal=[[Swiss Medical Weekly]]|volume=132|issue=7–8|pages=83–91|doi=10.4414/smw.2002.09939|issn=1424-7860|pmid=11971202|year=2002|s2cid=33386091 |doi-access=free}}</ref> for which he was the co-discoverer, in their functions of regulating lipid and glucose metabolism, inflammation, wound-healing, and cell differentiation processes. He also investigated the role of PPARs in the liver disease known as [[non-alcoholic fatty liver disease]] (NAFLD).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Jiapeng|last2=Montagner|first2=Alexandra|last3=Tan|first3=Nguan Soon|last4=Wahli|first4=Walter|title=Insights into the Role of PPARß/d in NAFLD|journal=International Journal of Molecular Sciences|language=en|volume=19|issue=7|pages=1893|doi=10.3390/ijms19071893|pmid=29954129|pmc=6073272|year=2018|doi-access=free}}</ref> He underscored the potential of PPARs as drug targets for NAFLD that is often associated to [[metabolic syndrome]] and [[type 2 diabetes]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Desvergne|first1=Béatrice|last2=Wahli|first2=Walter|date=1999-10-01|title=Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptors: Nuclear Control of Metabolism|journal=Endocrine Reviews|language=en|volume=20|issue=5|pages=649–688|doi=10.1210/edrv.20.5.0380|pmid=10529898|issn=0163-769X|doi-access=free}}</ref> Wahli obtained patents for his inventions. His patents include "Composition for regulating lipid metabolism" (2013)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Composition for regulating lipid metabolism|pubdate=2013-08-27|country=US|number=8518459|assign=Actigenomics SA|inventor1-last=Wahli|inventor1-first=Walter|inventor2-last=Bourgeois-Lugand|inventor2-first=Marie Françoise Yvonne|inventor3-last=Husson-Robert|inventor3-first=Bernadette|inventor4-last=Parisot|inventor4-first=Gilles Didier}}</ref> and "Composition for enhancing immunity" (2019).<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Composition for enhancing immunity|pubdate=2019-12-04|country=EP|number=3027056|assign=Actigenomics SA|inventor1-last=Bourgeois|inventor1-first=Marie Françoise|inventor2-last=Cefaï|inventor2-first=Daniel|inventor3-last=Wahli|inventor3-first=Walter|inventor4=Mireille Prince-David;Lisine Tuyisenge}}</ref>
